# Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the Boss — "The Central AI" from GDD §4.3. The scene should show its multi-phase health bar, 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases, and complex bullet patterns. This is the final challenge enemy with unique mechanics (multi-hit health, phase transitions).

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing boss behaviour — wants to see all boss attack phases, health bar, and bullet patterns in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of multi-phase boss behaviour with health bar management.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see the Boss cycle through 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases so I can verify the phase transition logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to see a 4-phase health bar that visually depletes as the Boss takes damage so I can verify the health bar rendering.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to deal damage to the Boss so I can test health bar progression and phase transitions.
- As a **developer**, I want to see clear visual and audio cues before each boss attack phase begins so I can verify the telegraphing system.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts`) renders the Boss enemy with all attack patterns.
- [ ] **AC2 — Boss visual style:** The Central AI renders as a large, imposing neon entity with a visible central core, consistent with a "boss" aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — Multi-phase health bar:** A 4-phase health bar is displayed; each phase depletes independently. The Boss cycles through 3–4 distinct attack patterns as health phases progress.
- [ ] **AC4 — Boss attack phases implemented:** All Boss phases from the GDD are present:
  - **Phase 1:** Spread — Boss fires bullets in a wide spread pattern.
  - **Phase 2:** Spiral — Bullets spiral outward from the Boss in a rotating pattern.
  - **Phase 3:** Pulse — Screen-wide pulse wave expands from the Boss, followed by aimed shots at the player's last known position.
  - **Phase 4 — Desperation:** All previous patterns combined at higher speed; Boss core becomes more exposed/bright (visual cue).
- [ ] **AC5 — Damage button:** A button on-screen deals damage to the Boss, advancing the health bar through phases. Visual cues (core exposure) change at each phase transition.
- [ ] **AC6 — Telegraphing:** Each attack phase begins with clear tell animations and advance audio cues (≥ 500 ms lead time) before the visual event.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript.
- **Gym scope:** This scene is a standalone gym scene (not shipped with the game) — no player ship, no other enemy types, no HUD beyond health bar, no power-ups.
- **Enemy behaviour:** The Boss is multi-hit (4 phases). Each phase has a distinct visual representation and attack pattern.
- **Phase transitions:** Visual cues (core exposure, brightness) indicate phase progression. Audio cues announce transitions.
- **Firing:** All Boss attack phases fire complex bullet patterns. Patterns should be learnable but increasingly difficult as phases progress.
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, each phase's unique audio cue, phase transitions, and destruction.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — The Boss gym scene.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — Boss enemy entity (multi-phase health + attack patterns).
- `src/assets/` — Boss sprite (large, imposing neon entity with core).
- `src/audio/` — Boss-related sound effects (spawn, phase cues, transitions, destruction).

## Related work

- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** — related; implements V-formation pattern.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related; will refactor code across enemy gym scenes.
- **Gym index scene (AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ)** — related; will link to this scene from the gym index.
- **Game Design Document (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — authoritative spec, §4.3 Boss Design (The Central AI).

## Best practices (mandatory — see docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md)

This scene MUST be built on the shared core gym formation-scene library and follow the conventions documented in **`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`** (see §3 "Best practice: adding a new enemy gym scene" and §5 "Extending the core library"). In particular:

- Extend `GymFormationScene` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts) wherever the scene is a formation-driven gym scene; supply only entity-specific configuration (`EnemyFormationConfig`), constants, and thin test accessors — DO NOT copy the ~200-line formation/UI/bullet boilerplate from the pre-refactor `GymScout`/`GymDiver`/`GymTank`.
- Movement that exceeds `applyFormationPosition()`'s flat-translation contract (e.g. E4 orbital paths, E5 clusters, Boss phases) belongs in the **entity** or as a new seam in the core library per §5 — never by duplicating scene boilerplate.
- Reuse the shared formation-offset builders in `src/utils/formations.ts` for any grid/formation geometry; add new pure builders there with unit tests.
- Follow the new-scene checklist: `add.existing()` for display-list membership, `lineStyle()` after `clear()` in entity drawing, exported tuning constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests (spawn count, geometry, drift, EXPLODE, SHOOT toggle, `← INDEX`).
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1/§3 if this scene introduces a new convention.

- [ ] **AC9 — Core library reuse:** The scene extends the shared `GymFormationScene` core library or its documented extension seam (§5 of `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) where applicable (Boss phase/health extensions may compose with the base class) and contains no duplicated formation/UI/bullet boilerplate.
- [ ] **AC10 — Guide compliance:** The implementation follows `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3–§5: `add.existing()`, `lineStyle()` after `clear()`, exported constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests.

# Player thruster SFX — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

The player ship has no thruster audio feedback. Thruster sound effects should rise continuously from silence to a sustained hum whose volume (and optionally pitch) is proportional to the ship's configured thrust acceleration value, so tuning the `thrustAcceleration` slider (GDD §2.2, `ShipConfig`) is legible by ear as well as by the animated flame.

## Users

- Player piloting the ship in any gym scene (either control scheme), relying on thruster hum to confirm thrust input and tuning changes without watching the flame.
- Developer tuning ship physics via the config sliders, hearing the acceleration change immediately.

## User Stories

- As a player holding a thrust key, I hear a thruster hum that fades in from silence so the onset of thrust is not a click/pop.
- As a player holding thrust at low `thrustAcceleration`, I hear a quieter/lower hum than at high `thrustAcceleration`, so the slider is audible.
- As a player releasing all thrust keys, I hear the hum decay quickly to silence, matching the flame shrink-back.
- As a player switching to the Asteroids scheme, forward thrust and turn thrust (side engines) produce the same thruster hum via the shared `getEngineSoundLevel` interface (VFX-matching key-specific behaviour stays visual-only; audio is a single ship-level hum).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Procedural thruster hum function(s):** `src/audio/effects.ts` exposes a thruster SFX interface (e.g. `startThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound`/`setThrusterLevel` or a single `updateThrusterSound(level: number)` that internally manages a sustained oscillator+gain) using Web Audio synthesis (no external assets). Distinct from all existing blip/cue sounds. Degrades to safe no-op without an AudioContext (headless tests, autoplay-blocked browsers).
- **AC2 — Level scales with acceleration value:** The audible level is 0 when not thrusting and rises to a configured maximum when thrusting, scaled by `ShipConfig.thrustAcceleration` (reference `FLAME_REF_THRUST = 300` / `DEFAULT_CONFIG.thrustAcceleration`). At `thrustAcceleration = 0` the hum stays silent (consistent with `flameGrowthRate` returning 0). Higher thrust reaches full volume faster and reads louder/higher — at minimum the gain is proportional to `thrustAcceleration / FLAME_REF_THRUST` (clamped to [0, 1]).
- **AC3 — Rise from nothing (fade-in) and quick decay:** When thrust begins, gain ramps from 0 to the target level over a short window (≤ 100 ms at reference thrust, faster at higher thrust — analogous to `FLAME_GROWTH_TIME_AT_REF = 30 ms`). When thrust stops, gain decays to 0 at ~4× the growth rate (mirroring `FLAME_SHRINK_MULTIPLIER = 4`), with no clicks/pops (gain envelope). Retriggering thrust while still decaying restarts the ramp from the current gain.
- **AC4 — Scheme-agnostic wiring via movement model:** `MovementModel.getEngineSoundLevel` returns a continuous level in [0, 1] for the SFX layer to consume (FourDirectional: 0 when no direction held, 1 when any thrust key held, scaled by acceleration; Asteroids: 0 when idle, 1 when forward/turnLeft/turnRight held, scaled similarly). Player or scene code drives the audio from the model's level each frame (e.g. `Player.preUpdate` or the active scene's update), without affecting physics (`tick` unchanged).
- **AC5 — No overlapping/orphaned audio:** Holding thrust does not stack multiple oscillators; releasing and re-pressing does not leak AudioNodes. Rapid toggling is clean. If the ship is destroyed/respawned or the scene switches, the hum stops.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests verify (a) the thruster audio node respects AudioContext absence (no-op), (b) `getEngineSoundLevel` returns 0 at idle and > 0 / scaled proportionally when thrusting (including thrust=0 edge case), (c) gain/volume ramping exists (e.g. gain envelope calls or oscillator lifecycle), and (d) scene/Player wiring drives the hum per frame while thrusting and silences it when idle. Full project test suite passes with no regressions.
- **AC7 — Documentation:** GDD §7.3 Audio Direction — Player Audio Character table updated with the thruster hum row (synthesis, wave, contour, volume, thrust-scaling note). Code comments document the thruster interface, thrust-scaling rationale, and autoplay/no-AudioContext fallback.
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no external audio assets (GDD §7.3).
- Safe no-op without AudioContext; respects browser autoplay policy (silent until user gesture).
- Must not introduce physics changes — `MovementModel.tick` and flame animation (`src/utils/flame.ts`) remain behaviourally unchanged; only `getEngineSoundLevel` and the audio integration change.
- Volume ceiling ≤ 0.2 to stay consistent with existing player cues (GDD §7.3 "All player cues keep volume ≤ 0.2").
- Backward compatible with both control schemes; does not regress existing VFX (per-engine flame) or shoot/pickup audio.

## Existing State

- `src/utils/movementModel.ts`: `getEngineSoundLevel` is a binary placeholder (returns 0 or 1) for both models; `getEngineActivity` is key-specific (AH-0MTFORPJ2003RWWQ). `flame.ts` already models growth ∝ `thrustAcceleration` with 30 ms to full at ref thrust and 4× decay.
- `src/audio/effects.ts`: 11+ procedural cues (enemy spawn/destruction, Tank/Scout/Diver, Swarm, player shoot/pickups) all via `blip()` or discrete oscillators; no continuous/looping hum and no thruster audio yet.
- `src/entities/Player.ts`: `preUpdate` animates per-engine flame lengths via `getEngineActivity` + `flame.ts`; no audio calls for thrusters. `ShipConfig.thrustAcceleration` defaults to 300 and is live-tunable via gym sliders.
- Docs: GDD §7.3 catalogs player shoot/pickup audio but has no thruster hum entry; §2.2 describes the flame scaling with `thrustAcceleration`.

## Desired Change

- `src/audio/effects.ts`: add a sustained thruster hum (e.g. low sawtooth/square + sine undertone, filtered hum) with an API that a per-frame caller can drive: create/reuse a single oscillator+gain pair, ramp gain from 0 to `level * maxVolume` (level ∈ [0, 1] from the movement model), and stop/cleanup on silence. Ensure exponential/linear gain ramps avoid clicks and the node lifecycle does not leak.
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts`: upgrade `getEngineSoundLevel` from binary to a continuous level scaled by `thrustAcceleration` (e.g. `level = (forward||turn||anyDir ? min(1, thrustAcceleration/FLAME_REF_THRUST) : 0)` or a dedicated param) — or document that the caller scales the binary level by the config value; keep `getEngineActivity` unchanged.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` (or active gym scenes): in `preUpdate`/scene update, derive the current thruster level from `getEngineSoundLevel` + config and call the audio interface each frame; ensure the hum follows the pressed keys (4-dir: any arrow/WASD; Asteroids: W/Up, A/Left, D/Right) and stops when the model reports 0.
- Tests: `src/utils/movementModel.test.ts`, `src/audio/effects.test.ts`, and Player/scene tests updated to assert scaling, no-op, and wiring.
- Docs: GDD §7.3 and inline comments updated.

## Key Files

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Needs sustained thruster hum with thrust-scaled gain/pitch and safe no-op
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — Needs `getEngineSoundLevel` upgraded to continuous [0,1] scaled by thrustAcceleration
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Needs per-frame audio driving from model level (preUpdate integration); verify no physics change
- `src/utils/flame.ts` — Reference for thrust-proportional growth/decay model (reuse timing constants analogously)
- `src/core/config.ts` — ShipConfig.thrustAcceleration source of scaling; no change expected (read-only)
- `src/utils/movementModel.test.ts` — Needs thruster-level unit tests (binary→scaled, thrust=0 edge)
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Needs thruster hum oscillator/gain + no-op tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 Player Audio Character — Needs thruster hum row + scaling note

## Related Work

- **AH-0MTFORPJ2003RWWQ** — Asteroids directional VFX improvements (key-specific flame selection; `getEngineSoundLevel` placeholder — direct interface to extend)
- **AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU** — Player has no audio (shoot + pickup procedural cues — established `effects.ts` Web Audio patterns and GDD §7.3 Player Audio Character table)
- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** — Alternative player control (pluggable movement models, 3-engine layout, `getEngineSoundLevel` origin Q4)
- **AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S** — Gym scene with player ship and thrust-based movement (flame VFX, `ShipConfig`)
- **AH-0MTAF5YLT009TXAM** — Thrust flame scales with `thrustAcceleration` (flame.ts growth model — direct scaling precedent)
- **AH-0MTGS4P0V005MTSN** — Add 4 player shoot audio cues (wave-type distinctiveness precedent — thruster hum must stay distinct)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scaling basis assumption:** "acceleration value" is interpreted as `ShipConfig.thrustAcceleration` (not velocity or instantaneous force). Gain/pitch thus scales with the config slider; idle = silent, max ≈ 0.15–0.2. If the producer meant a different acceleration metric, the scaling factor can be swapped with minimal code change.
- **Single hum vs per-engine hums:** Assumed single ship-level hum (not one oscillator per engine port). Per-engine layering would complicate mixing and is out of scope; can be added as a follow-up if side-thruster distinctiveness is desired.
- **Continuous vs discrete:** Assumed sustained oscillator+gain (not repeated blips) to meet "rise from nothing" — requires careful AudioNode lifecycle to avoid leaks. Mitigation: single reused node with gain ramping + unit tests for cleanup.
- **Autoplay/silent-until-gesture:** Hum will be silent until the first user interaction (browser policy) — same as all other SFX; documented in GDD §7.3.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Per-engine spatialisation, pitch-bend on velocity, or background music integration are out of scope — track as `discovered-from:AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620` work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- Q1 — Scaling basis: "rise from nothing to thruster sound based on the acceleration value" — should the audible level scale with (a) `ShipConfig.thrustAcceleration` (the tuning slider, analogous to flame growth), (b) instantaneous thrust input (binary held/released), (c) current ship velocity, or (d) a combination? Assumed (a) scaled by held-state (binary × config ratio) — confirm or correct. — Answer: *(open — assumed (a); awaiting producer confirmation)* Source: intake assumption; reference `src/core/config.ts:DEFAULT_CONFIG.thrustAcceleration`, `src/utils/flame.ts:flameGrowthRate`.
- Q2 — Hum character: Should the thruster be a continuous looping hum/drone (sustained oscillator with gain ramp) or a one-shot sweep per thrust press? Should it differ between forward vs turn thrust? Assumed continuous single hum with gain ramp, not per-engine distinct tones — confirm. — Answer: *(open — assumed continuous single hum)* Source: intake assumption; reference GDD §7.3 procedural approach, `src/audio/effects.ts` existing continuous cues (Tank whine).
- Q3 — Integration scope: Which scenes should hear the hum — every scene that hosts the player (all gyms + future combat scenes) or a single gym first? Assumed Player-driven in `Player.preUpdate` so every host scene inherits it — confirm scope and whether a mute/volume setting should apply. — Answer: *(open — assumed Player-preUpdate, all host scenes,≤ 0.2 volume)* Source: intake assumption; reference `src/entities/Player.ts:preUpdate`, `src/scenes/gym/*`.

# Fix tree_coverage helper reading children from wrong JSON key

## Summary
The shared plan-skill helper _wl_show_children (skills/shared/tree_coverage.py) reads data['workItem']['children'], but `wl show <id> --children --json` returns the children list at the TOP level (data['children']), alongside 'workItem'. As a result run_coverage_review sees zero children and reports vacuous 100% coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. _wl_show_children returns the top-level 'children' list from wl show --children --json.
2. run_coverage_review reports real child AC coverage (child_summary populated).
3. Existing tests for tree_coverage pass (updated if they encoded the wrong shape).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a work item with children.
2. Run python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared'); import tree_coverage as tc; print(tc._wl_show_children('<id>'))" — returns [] even though wl show --children --json returns the children.

## Notes
- discovered-from:AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC (plan run exposed the bug; workaround applied via monkeypatch).
- File: /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/shared/tree_coverage.py (~line 145).
- Agent infrastructure (.pi/agent/skills) — do not edit without explicit authorisation.

# GymSwarm AC3 (swarm aimed fire hits player) is flaky under full-suite parallel load — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

`GymSwarm.test.ts > AC3 — a player bullet destroys a swarm member; a swarm shot hitting the player respawns it` failed once during the implement finish-gate full-suite run for AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ (14 tests | 1 failed, 156 ms — not a timeout) while all ad-hoc full-suite runs (4× 526/526) passed. The transient burst/hit state is missed under parallel CPU load when the test relies on a single interval-boundary clock jump and a single volley's random spread.

## Users

- **CI / developer** — wants `npm --silent test` to be deterministic under full-suite parallel load, so a passing gate means the same on retry — not a one-off flake that erodes trust in gym coverage.
  - *Story:* As a developer running the gate, I run the full suite once and the verdict is stable, so I don't chase false failures.
- **Gym playtester / gym maintainer** — wants AC3 to faithfully prove swarm aimed fire can hit and respawn the player, not merely that one lucky volley happened to land.
  - *Story:* As a playtester, I trust AC3 as a specification: swarm bursts are aimed at the live player and a hit causes destruction + respawn + invulnerability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — AC3 deterministic under parallel load:** `GymSwarm.test.ts > AC3` does not depend on a single `scene.time.now += SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL + 500` boundary jump; it polls with bounded quarter-interval clock steps so the swarm re-fires fresh aimed volleys until one lands (mirrors the GymScout AC2 fix in commit `e48b046`), and passes reliably under `npm --silent test` (full-suite parallel). *At current HEAD the per-enemy GymSwarm scene is retired into `GymEnemies` (enemyKey=swarm) — see Key Files — so this AC is satisfied by the landed poll fix at `38fddc6` and its preserved semantics in `Swarm` + `GymFormationScene`.*
- **AC2 — Hit semantics preserved:** After the player bullet destroys one swarm member (`aliveCount` decrements, victim `bodyVisible` false, bullet consumed), a subsequent swarm burst that reaches the player increments `getPlayerHitCount()`, respawns the player at `PLAYER_SPAWN`, sets `isPlayerInvulnerable() === true`, and `playDestructionSound` is called.
- **AC3 — No single-volley luck dependency:** The hit poll is bounded (e.g. ≤160 quarter-interval steps) but never asserts on the first volley's random spread (`±0.15 rad` per bullet); comments measure/document the ~12% all-miss rate at full-suite load that the poll guards against.
- **AC4 — Validation/tests:** `npm --silent test` passes and remains stable across repeated full-suite runs (at least 3 consecutive greens at the fix commit); no production behaviour changed — only test determinism.
- **AC5 — Documentation:** Code comments explain the spread-vs-poll rationale and the mirror to `e48b046`; no README/wiki change required beyond those comments (production behaviour unchanged).

## Constraints

- Small, chore-scope test-hardening only: no production logic change (Swarm firing cadence and aim remain unchanged); no new behaviour or scene refactor.
- Keep the bound tight: poll loop must terminate deterministically (bounded steps, no wall-clock `setTimeout` wait).
- Follows the established gym flake pattern (`c2aaa54` GymDiver AC1, `e48b046` GymScout AC2, `38fddc6` GymSwarm AC3/GymTank AC3) — deterministic `tick(dt)` + frozen `scene.time.now` advancement.
- Do not block on Enemy Design tooling (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN); this is a standalone stability fix.

## Existing state

- At HEAD the fix for this exact flake has already landed as part of `AH-0MTFU1GAO009KDBM` (`38fddc6`, on `dev` and ancestor of `HEAD`): `GymSwarm.test.ts` AC3 no longer does a single `+ SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL + 500` jump; it captures `hitsBefore = getPlayerHitCount()` and loops `for (…; i<160 && hitCount===hitsBefore; i++) { scene.time.now += SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL/4; scene.tick(0.05); }` so fresh aimed volleys re-fire until one lands — exactly the GymScout AC2 poll idiom (`e48b046`). The pre-fix single-volley window missed hits at ~12% of volleys at full-suite load.
- Parent epic AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC (`Player cannot be moved in enemy/power-up gyms`) is `done` at `38fddc6` with suite green (31 files, 543 tests), and its flake siblings `GymDiver AC1` (`c2aaa54`) and `GymScout AC2` (`e48b046`) are on `dev`.
- GymTank AC3's companion wall-clock flake was fixed the same commit by driving drift via accumulated `tick(dt)` instead of `setTimeout`.
- Per-enemy gym scenes (`GymSwarm`, `GymScout`, `GymTank`, `GymDiver`, etc.) were retired at `5bbaa2d` into the single config-driven `GymEnemies` scene (enemyKey=swarm/scout/tank/…) backed by `GymFormationScene`. At current HEAD (`495b26b`) the AC3 semantics are covered by `src/entities/Swarm.test.ts` (burst/aim) + `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` (hit→respawn+invulnerability). Production burst constants remain in `src/entities/Swarm.ts` (`SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL = 900`, `SWARM_BULLET_SPEED = 180`).

## Desired change

- Harden `GymSwarm.test.ts` AC3 to the deterministic poll form described in AC1 (if not already at HEAD, apply it; if already at HEAD, verify and formalise as the acceptance contract) so the test never depends on one random-spread volley.
- Keep the bounded hit window (or lengthen only if needed for stability) and add/retain comments explaining the spread-vs-poll rationale and the mirror to `e48b046`.
- Verify with repeated full-suite runs (`≥3` consecutive `npm --silent test` greens) and leave a comment linking the prior failure, the fix commits, and the verification.
- *Note at current HEAD:* the desired poll is already on `dev` history (`38fddc6`) and the file is retired; the contract is preserved by retaining the Swarm + GymFormationScene coverage — no new file edits required unless a regression is found during verification.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — burst constants `SWARM_BURST_INTERVAL`, `SWARM_BULLET_SPEED` and `tryFireBurstBullet` spread contract (±0.15 rad)
- `src/entities/Swarm.test.ts` — Swarm entity unit tests (burst interval, aimed fire, destruction, formation)
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — shared formation base: burst collection, hit/respawn + invulnerability, deterministic `tick(dt)` + live aim seam
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — core scene AC3 coverage (enemy bullet hits player → `getPlayerHitCount`/respawn/`isPlayerInvulnerable` + blink)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — config-driven swarm gym (enemyKey=swarm) wiring Swarm into GymFormationScene (retired GymSwarm.ts at `5bbaa2d`)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — GymEnemies smoke/config tests (retired GymSwarm.test.ts heritage)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.test.ts` (historical, retired at `5bbaa2d`) — reference poll idiom (`e48b046`: `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL` + quarter-cue steps) — see git history
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.test.ts` (historical, retired at `5bbaa2d`) — companion deterministic drift fix (`38fddc6`) — reference only

## Related work

- **AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC** — `Player cannot be moved in enemy and power-up gym scenes` (parent epic, `done` at `38fddc6`; scheme-aware gym work that first surfaced this one-off)
- **AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ** — `Scheme-aware input tests for affected gym scenes` (finish-gate run where this AC3 first failed once)
- **AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C** — `GymScout.test.ts is flaky under full-suite parallel load` (sibling flake epic; describes GymSwarm AC3/GymTank AC3/GymDiver AC1 fixes and their expected verifications; `done` at `38fddc6`)
- **AH-0MTFU1GAO009KDBM** — `fix flaky timer-sensitive gym tests` (`38fddc6`: landed the GymSwarm AC3 poll + GymTank drift fixes; verified 3× full-suite green)
- **AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW** — `GymDiver AC1 (diver x locked during dive) is wall-clock flaky` (deterministic `tick` pattern `c2aaa54`, mirrored here)
- Commit `e48b046` — `GymScout AC2` quarter-cue poll idiom (pattern mirrored for Swarm)
- Commit `c2aaa54` — `GymDiver AC1` deterministic rewrite (pattern mirrored for Tank/Swarm)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: fix already landed but brief stale.** Mitigation: intake formalises the *contract* (poll, not single jump) so future edits cannot regress it; at current HEAD the contract is preserved via `Swarm` + `GymFormationScene` after the `5bbaa2d` retirement — verify via those tests.
- **Risk: hidden timing coupling (Phaser `time.now` vs real loop).** Mitigation: keep frozen-clock advancement (`scene.time.now += …`) + `tick(0.05)` only — no `setTimeout` waits.
- **Risk: over-lengthening the window masks a real aim bug.** Mitigation: AC2 keeps directional assertions (mean burst aims at `PLAYER_SPAWN`); poll bounds remain tight (≤160 steps).
- **Risk: scope creep into Swarm production tuning.** Mitigation: explicitly out of scope — only the test hardens.
- **Assumption:** Intake may proceed without operator Q&A — the failure mode, proposed fix, and reference commits are explicit in the item; reasonable assumptions documented here.
- **Assumption:** Operator permits proceeding without further questions (prompt allows recording open questions and marking `needs-producer-review` only if blocked — not blocked here).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- No interview round was run — the seed item already contains the failure observation (`156 ms`, not a timeout; `4× 526/526` ad-hoc greens), the root-cause hypothesis (single boundary jump + single random-spread volley + bounded 8 s hit window; ~12% all-miss at load), and the proposed fix topology (poll for burst, as in `e48b046`, and/or lengthen window). Research inspected: `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.test.ts` at HEAD, `src/entities/Swarm.ts` constants, commits `e48b046`/`c2aaa54`/`38fddc6`, and related items AH-0MTFSM3IR001QR0C / AH-0MTFPDKDU006QUDC / AH-0MTFRQR42001M8WQ / AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW. If the producer prefers a different stability threshold (e.g. more/fewer full-suite repetitions or a different bound) that can be adjusted at plan/implement with no brief change.

# When all enemies in enemy gym scene have been killed respawn them (AH-0MTFXKA5Q003LBH5)

## Problem statement

Enemy gym scenes (`GymScout`, `GymDiver`, `GymTank`, `GymPhaser`, `GymSwarm`) allow the player to destroy every enemy (1 HP each, `alive === false` after `destroySelf()`), leaving an empty field with nothing to do. When the formation is fully cleared, start a visible 3-second countdown and then respawn the full formation so the gym remains usable without reloading the scene.

## Users

- **Player / tester exercising an enemy gym** — wants continuous targets to practice flight, aiming, and weapon feel without manually refreshing the scene.
- **Developer / AI agent verifying enemy behaviour** — wants a deterministic, observable wipe → countdown → respawn loop that can be asserted in automated tests.

### Example user stories

- As a **player in any enemy gym**, when I destroy the last alive enemy, I see a 3-second countdown (e.g. centred `Respawning in 3…2…1…`) and then a fresh formation appears at its starting position so I can keep shooting.
- As a **developer**, I want the wipe detection and respawn to live in the shared core (`GymFormationScene`) so all five formation gyms inherit it without per-scene duplication, and the behaviour is covered by scene tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Wipe detection and 3s countdown:** When `aliveCount` transitions to `0` (all `FormationSceneEntity.alive === false`), the scene starts a 3-second countdown and displays a visible countdown indicator (text overlay). The countdown ticks once per second and is observable for tests (getter or text contents).
- [ ] **AC2 — Automatic respawn after countdown:** After exactly 3 seconds (within tick tolerance), the full formation respawns: `aliveCount` returns to `config.count`, entities reappear at `config.startX/startY`-derived positions, formation base resets to its start, and the countdown indicator is removed. `playSpawnSound()` (or equivalent) is triggered on respawn. Enemy bullets in flight are cleared so a stale bullet does not instantly hit the player.
- [ ] **AC3 — Applies to all formation gyms via the core library:** `GymScout`, `GymDiver`, `GymTank`, `GymPhaser`, `GymSwarm` all exhibit AC1–AC2 with no per-scene duplication beyond config. The change is implemented in `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (new fields/methods optional and backward compatible). `GymBoss` (multi-phase boss, separate scene) is out of scope unless explicitly noted.
- [ ] **AC4 — Combat and chrome preserved:** Player ship (arrows + WASD), `EXPLODE` / `SHOOT: ON/OFF` buttons, status/hint lines, drift/respawn off the right edge, and existing collision/explosion VFX/SFX behaviour remain unchanged except for the wipe→respawn addition. `shootEnabled` state carries over across the respawn (no surprise toggle).
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing and full suite:** Automated tests cover wipe detection, countdown progression (including that the countdown restarts correctly if the scene is torn down), successful respawn with correct positions/count, bullet cleanup on respawn, and that the existing `GymFormationScene` / per-gym tests still pass. Full project test suite passes (`npm test`).
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation:** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` updated to document the wipe → 3s countdown → respawn convention (including that it is core-library owned); related comments updated.

## Constraints

- No game-over, lives, or scoring changes — gyms remain demo/testbeds (infinite lives, as with player hit/respawn at `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE = 1.5s`).
- No collision engine — continue manual distance checks for any new collision-adjacent work.
- Prefer core-library extension over per-scene boilerplate; keep `EnemyFormationConfig` backward compatible.
- Use existing sounds (`src/audio/effects.ts`) and existing entity `destroySelf()`/`alive` contract; do not introduce a new entity type.

## Existing state

- Five enemy gyms are thin `GymFormationScene<TEntity,TBullet>` subclasses driven by `EnemyFormationConfig` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`): formation spawn, HUD buttons, status/hint/`← INDEX`, drift + `_respawnX()` off the right edge, per-entity `applyFormationPosition()`, fire-bullet collection + advance + cull, player spawn/input/auto-fire/bullet lifecycle/collisions/invulnerability blink.
- Enemies are 1 HP; destroying the last one leaves `aliveCount === 0` with no recovery — the scene stays empty indefinitely.
- Existing tests live in `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/Gym*.test.ts`; player hit/respawn is already covered (explosion VFX, `respawn()`, blink).

## Desired change

- Extend `GymFormationScene` to detect `aliveCount === 0`, start and tick a 3-second countdown (visible text, deterministic via `tick(dt)`), then on expiry clear enemy bullets, destroy/recreate or resurrect the formation at its initial geometry, reset `formationBaseX/Y` to `startX/Y`, refresh `statusText`, hide the countdown, and play the spawn sound. Expose minimal test seams (e.g. `isRespawnCountdownActive()`, `getRespawnCountdownRemaining()` or equivalent).
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §2–§3 to note the wipe/respawn lifecycle.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Add wipe detection, 3s countdown state/tick, countdown text overlay, bullet cleanup, and formation respawn logic; expose test getters.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Add AC1–AC3 tests for the core library.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts` (and `GymDiver.ts`, `GymTank.ts`, `GymPhaser.ts`, `GymSwarm.ts`) — No code change expected, but verify via per-scene smoke/regression tests that the core behaviour is inherited.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Document the wipe → countdown → respawn convention.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Reuse `playSpawnSound()` on respawn (no change unless a distinct sound is desired).

## Related work

- **AH-0MTD0Z0Y7003T1NT** — Add player to each Enemy Gym scene (completed, parent of the combat interactions `destroySelf()`/`alive` that define "killed").
- **AH-0MTECNG8W00403EH / AH-0MTECNG4K0071TIB** — Core scene: collision detection and player hit/respawn (establishes `aliveCount`, manual collisions, `Player.respawn()` pattern to reuse).
- **AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3 / AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9 / AH-0MTAN4T0I004H187** — Core-library extraction and rewrites that make this a one-place change.
- **AH-0MT99* family** — `Create E1–E5 Enemy Gym Scene` items (consumers of the core contract).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Killed" means `alive === false` after `destroySelf()` (including explosion VFX still playing) — i.e. `aliveCount === 0` is the wipe signal, not graphics lifecycle. Mitigation: state this explicitly and assert on `aliveCount`.
- **Assumption:** 3s countdown is wall-clock seconds driven by `tick(dt)` / `time.now`, not frames, and is **visible** to the player (centred countdown text). If the producer prefers a silent timer or a different presentation, adjust the overlay without changing the timing contract. Recorded as open clarification below.
- **Assumption:** Respawn resets the formation to `startX/startY` with the original `count/spacing` geometry and clears enemy bullets only (player bullets persist). If producer wants player bullets cleared or score/status preservation, note as follow-up.
- **Risk:** Countdown races with the formation drift `_respawnX()` (right-edge respawn) — they are orthogonal. Mitigation: wipe/respawn resets `formationBaseX/Y` and does not interfere with the drift timer.
- **Risk:** Scope creep — adding scoring waves, lives, or boss waves. Mitigation: this item is strictly wipe → 3s → same formation; any wave/score work goes to a linked follow-up.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the 3-second countdown be visible to the player, and if so where/how (e.g. centred text `Respawning in 3…`, status line countdown, both)?" — Answer: **Assumed visible centred countdown text** (e.g. `Respawning in 3…` ticking to `1…`) plus status line update; change presentation if producer prefers differently. Source: researcher inference from seed text ("3 second countdown") — no prior worklog entry specifies presentation; left as producer-reviewable assumption.
- Q: "On respawn, should the formation reset to `startX/startY` (as on initial `create()`) or continue from its current drift position? Should `shootEnabled` and any per-entity state be preserved or reset?" — Answer: **Assumed full reset to start position with `shootEnabled` preserved**, fresh entities (or resurrected) at initial offsets. Source: prior gym convention (spawn at `startX/startY`) and minimal-surprise principle; flagged for producer confirmation.
- Q: "Should enemy bullets (and/or player bullets) be cleared when the countdown ends and the formation respawns?" — Answer: **Assumed enemy bullets cleared, player bullets kept**. Source: prevents a stale enemy bullet from hitting the freshly respawned player; avoids surprising the player by deleting their shots. Flagged for producer review.
- Q: "Does this apply to `GymBoss` or only the five formation gyms? Does 'killed' include mid-explosion (`alive === false` but explosion animating) or only after animation completes?" — Answer: **Assumed formation gyms only (`GymScout`/`GymDiver`/`GymTank`/`GymPhaser`/`GymSwarm`); 'killed' = `aliveCount === 0` (mid-explosion counts)**. Source: Boss is multi-phase and tracked separately (`AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE` family); `alive` contract from `GymFormationScene`.

# Implement: Wipe detection, 3s countdown, and respawn in GymFormationScene (AH-0MTCORE01)

## Summary

Extend GymFormationScene to detect when all enemies are destroyed (aliveCount === 0), show a 3-second visible countdown, then respawn the full formation at its starting position.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 - Wipe detection:** When aliveCount transitions to 0 (all enemies alive === false), the scene immediately enters the respawn countdown state.
- [ ] **AC2 - 3s visible countdown:** A centered text overlay displays "Respawning in 3...", "Respawning in 2...", "Respawning in 1...", ticking once per second. The countdown is driven by tick(dt) with wall-clock seconds.
- [ ] **AC3 - Automatic respawn:** After exactly 3 seconds, the full formation respawns: all entities recreated at config.startX/startY-derived positions, formationBaseX/Y reset, aliveCount returns to config.count, countdown text removed.
- [ ] **AC4 - Bullet cleanup:** On respawn, all enemy bullets in flight are destroyed and cleared. Player bullets persist.
- [ ] **AC5 - Sound & state:** playSpawnSound() is called on respawn. shootEnabled state carries over (preserved across respawn).
- [ ] **AC6 - Test seams:** Expose isRespawnCountdownActive(): boolean and getRespawnCountdownRemaining(): number as public getters for test observation.
- [ ] **AC7 - No breaking changes:** All existing gym scenes continue to work unchanged; existing tests still pass.

## Implementation Notes

- Add new fields to GymFormationScene: private respawnCountdown = 0, private isRespawning = false, private countdownText: Phaser.GameObjects.Text
- In tick(dt): after the existing drift/bullet logic, check if aliveCount === 0 and not already respawning - set isRespawning = true, respawnCountdown = 3, create/hide the countdown text overlay.
- During countdown: decrement respawnCountdown by dt; update countdownText each second to show "Respawning in {N}...".
- When respawnCountdown <= 0: destroy old entities (call destroy() on each), clear this.bullets, recreate the formation via config.buildOffsets() + config.createEntity() loop (same as create()), reset formationBaseX/Y, hide countdown text, play playSpawnSound().
- The countdown overlay should be positioned at GAME_WIDTH/2, GAME_HEIGHT/2 with appropriate style matching gym HUD.
- EnemyFormationConfig is backward compatible - no new required fields.

## Key Files

- src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts - Add wipe detection, countdown state/tick, overlay text, bullet cleanup, formation respawn logic, and test getters.

## Dependencies

- None - this is the core implementation work item.
